clue.text: Comments as Seinfeld character recalled debut in sitcom

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the character's name is read back to front

parts.note: Cosmo Kramer, Jerry's eccentric neighbour in the US sitcom Seinfeld

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of sitcom

explanation.surface: A critic's comments about a Seinfeld character fondly remembered from the sitcom's opening episode.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks are spoken or written observations, a plain synonym for comments.

clue.text: Way to describe all possible outcomes of Braverman and tabloid both wanting leadership to change

definitions.text: Way to describe all possible outcomes

indicators.note: the remaining letters must change their order to form something new
each of the two words lacks its leader, meaning its first letter is dropped

parts.note: Suella Braverman, the former UK Home Secretary; her surname is used as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid and a right-wing politician both clamouring for a change of party leader, with every outcome on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the B of Braverman and the T of tabloid, then rearrange the fourteen letters left. Suella Braverman is a British Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics a random variable assigns a value to each possible result of an experiment, so it describes the whole set of outcomes.

clue.text: Tiny detail — from motorway, head on to A1 northbound

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, written with I for 1
nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: in a down entry, travelling north means reading upward, so the road name runs backwards

parts.note: A1 with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A traffic bulletin about joining the A1 heading north from a motorway, head on.
explanation.walkthrough: Motorway is the M1 (London to Leeds), not just M; the A1 is the Great North Road, so northbound suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutia is the singular of minutiae, a small or trivial particular, so it is a tiny detail.

clue.text: Prince maybe offensive to describe colour

parts.note: a prince is an example of a royal
blue means rude or obscene, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Prince, the singer, might be offensive in how he describes a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid shade of the colour blue.

clue.text: Regretful after making case of rubber goods wet

indicators.note: making one thing into another means replacing those letters with the new ones
a case is the outer covering, so only the first and last letters of the next word are meant

parts.note: sorry means feeling regret
the outside letters of rubber
G is short for good, so two of them are goods

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry once a cargo of rubber goods has been soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: In SORRY the two Rs, which are the case of rubber, become GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggy means thoroughly soaked, so it describes something wet.

clue.text: Happy to run around ship

indicators.note: around means the verb's letters go on either side of the vessel's letters

parts.note: colours run, or bleed, in the wash
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at the chance to jog round a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Run is the verb for dye spreading in the wash, not jogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed can mean fortunate and contented, a near synonym of happy.

clue.text: Public essentially find cycling over the hill without being able to see …

indicators.note: cycling round means the front letter is moved to the back of the word
the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letters are taken

parts.note: the middle two letters of public
find with its first letter carried round to the end
over the hill means past one's prime, old

explanation.surface: An ageing cyclist struggling over a hill, eyes shut, as the public rarely do.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something blindfold is to do it with the eyes covered, unable to see, as in playing chess blindfold.

clue.text: … a source of inspiration — regularly see reaction

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a blindfolded person finds inspiration by watching others' reactions.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, and the Muses were the classical sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Patient in cast massaged with oil

indicators.note: massaged means kneaded and worked over, so the letters are pushed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital patient with a limb in plaster being rubbed down with oil.
explanation.walkthrough: Patient looks like a noun for a hospital case, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoical means enduring hardship without complaint, much the same as patient.

clue.text: Feature of Oxford University Press I'm reading for revision

indicators.note: a revision reworks text into a new version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor at Oxford University Press reading a manuscript for revisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford University Press is a real publisher, so the eye reads it as one name; the split falls after University.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold called Oxford the city of dreaming spires, after the college towers and steeples on its skyline.

clue.text: Mug from New York hotel is breaking

indicators.note: something breaking into a pair of letters splits them apart and sits between

parts.note: NY is the standard abbreviation
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A souvenir mug from a New York hotel getting smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is a gullible fool, and a ninny is a silly, foolish person.

clue.text: Act unaided and aim to drink vermouth before lunchtime?

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so the target word holds the other one

parts.note: a goal is an aim
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
one o'clock is lunchtime

explanation.surface: Someone deciding to drink vermouth alone before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Before means this time comes after the rest, as the question mark warns: it is one o'clock that the drinking precedes.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for doing something independently, without help.

clue.text: Published work by journalist performed better

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a play is a dramatic work
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist's published work outshines the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay someone is to perform better than them in a game.

clue.text: Philosopher backing computer company

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the words are read right to left

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A philosopher providing financial backing for a tech firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing looks like investing, but it reverses the computer and the company together.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam was the medieval English philosopher behind Occam's razor.

clue.text: Commotion as friend gets house during bingo on vacation

indicators.note: during places these within the span of what follows
vacated means emptied, so the middle of the word is removed and its outside letters remain

parts.note: the first of bingo's outer letters
an ally is a friend
HO is short for house
the last of bingo's outer letters

explanation.surface: An uproar at a holiday bingo hall when a pal wins a full house.
explanation.walkthrough: Full house is the winning call in bingo, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or sensational publicity, so it is a commotion.

clue.text: Really funny greeting — different opening is ten times bigger

indicators.note: the first letter, read as a Roman numeral, is swapped for the numeral worth ten times as much

parts.note: hi is a greeting
various means different, as in various kinds

explanation.surface: A greeting card joke that gets ten times bigger with a different opening line.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral 5 and L is 50, so V becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarious means extremely amusing, a stronger synonym of very funny.

clue.text: Almost stumbled on crook

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to stumble is to fall; past tense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who nearly tripped over a criminal, or a shepherd's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumbled on looks like a phrasal verb, but on is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a criminal, and a felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: Diet including brewed ales and hot pork pie

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the diet word wraps round the rest

parts.note: diet is the food one eats

indicators.note: brewing stirs and ferments ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A diet that somehow allows beer and a hot pork pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie, often cut to porky; it looks like part of the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is an untrue statement, and pork pie is British rhyming slang for exactly that.

clue.text: See 1
Write copy about extremely philosophical computer company

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the copying word is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of philosophical

explanation.surface: Instructions to a writer to produce copy on a philosophical computer firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Write seems to serve the surface only, as an instruction to produce copy. The clue pairs with 12-across, whose wordplay used the Mac.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple is the American technology company that makes the Mac and the iPhone.

clue.text: School year's separating in games — daughter's excited

indicators.note: something separating a word splits it and sits in the gap
in places the combined piece inside the games word

parts.note: the first half of PE, physical education, school games
the start of SCH, the abbreviation for school
Y is short for year
the end of SCH
the second half of PE
D is short for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter thrilled that her school year is being split up for games.
explanation.walkthrough: Y splits SCH to give SYCH, which then goes inside PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyched is informal for excited or mentally keyed up.

clue.text: Intermittently clear day with nothing on, sweetheart

indicators.note: intermittently means on and off, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
love is nothing in tennis scoring, placed on the end

explanation.surface: Sunbathing naked with a partner on a day that keeps clearing up.
explanation.walkthrough: With nothing on hints at nudity, but nothing is the zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladylove is an old-fashioned word for a woman who is someone's beloved, so a sweetheart.

clue.text: Desert — perhaps at speed it sounds like dessert after volume's adjusted initially

indicators.note: after sends the sound-alike second, behind the volume and its companion letter

parts.note: V is short for volume

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of adjusted

indicators.note: sounds like says the piece is spelt as another word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: a mousse is a dessert; a moose is the large deer said the same way

explanation.surface: A pun about desert versus dessert, with the volume turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: After puts the sound-alike after the two letters. Desert is the verb, abandon, not the sandy noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leave in a hurry, so it means to desert, especially quickly.

clue.text: See 8
Ultimately celery has plastic Lidl wrapping that depicts simple rural scene

indicators.note: wrapping goes round the outside, so the rearranged shop name encloses the other letter
plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written; Lidl is a German discount supermarket chain

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of the vegetable is taken

parts.note: the last letter of celery

explanation.surface: Supermarket celery sold in plastic wrapping with a picture of a farm scene on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a picturesque, peaceful pastoral scene, or a poem describing one.

clue.text: Dictator's tax enlarged Bank of America?

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone who dictates, speaking words aloud for another to write

parts.note: a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: A tyrant imposes a tax increase on a big American bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Dictator suggests a tyrant, but it means a person dictating. Bank of America is a real bank; here it is a riverbank, as the question mark signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is a raised embankment built along a river, a term used chiefly in the US, so a built-up American bank.

clue.text: Help for the poor old woman with parking — an outstanding plan

parts.note: poor relief was historic aid to the needy
old woman is slang for mother, ma
P for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A welfare scheme for the poor and an elderly woman's parking: what a great plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Outstanding looks like praise, but it means standing out, raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows the land's height with raised or shaded contours, so its features literally stand out.

clue.text: Burglar vanishes, hiding grub

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so the letters are tucked within the words before

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A burglar escapes, concealing some food on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub looks like food, the sense the burglar story suggests, but here it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft-bodied young stage of an insect, which is a larva.

clue.text: Conduct review of unrestricted river harbour after docking

indicators.note: reviewing something means going over it afresh, so these letters are reorganised
with its restricting boundaries gone, the word loses its first and last letters
docking a tail cuts off its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Conducting a survey of a free-flowing river and of a harbour once ships have docked.
explanation.walkthrough: Conduct looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour is how someone acts, a direct synonym of conduct as a noun.

clue.text: Remote university holding party — get tip for beer pong

indicators.note: holding means having it inside, so the university letters go round the party

parts.note: the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
a do is a party

indicators.note: a tip is an end point, here the far end of the word

parts.note: the final letter of beer

explanation.surface: Students at a university party getting tips for beer pong, the drinking game.
explanation.walkthrough: Beer pong looks like one phrase, but pong is the definition: British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a stink, and an odour is a smell, usually an unpleasant one.

clue.text: Some attend lessons non-stop

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: Pupils who attend lessons continuously.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means without end or pause, the same as non-stop.

clue.text: Speak to 10 Downing Street for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to talk to formally

explanation.surface: Delivering a speech at the British Prime Minister's official residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Downing Street is the London home of the British Prime Minister, and here it is just an example of where someone lives.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them, and an address is a street location such as Number 10.
